title: How to Stick with Good Habits Every Day
coreMove: Use visible tracking to return quickly after a miss instead of worshiping the streak.
sourcePressure: Visible evidence and habit tracking can make repetition satisfying across days, but the practical recovery rule is to avoid missing twice in a row.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Turning tracking into perfectionism, shame, or streak worship.

hook: starting with a definition of habit tracking
counterintuition: the problem is not motivation alone

exampleSpecs.domain: a beekeeper tracking hive inspections with colored pins and returning after one missed day
exampleSpecs.audience: a hobbyist tempted to abandon the log after travel
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether visible tracking creates return rather than shame
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she places a yellow pin for the missed inspection and schedules the next check instead of ripping down the board
exampleSpecs.firstImage: colored pins on a hive map board

exampleSpecs.domain: a public-radio producer marking daily tape reviews with cassette stickers
exampleSpecs.audience: a producer learning to hear cleaner edits
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the tracker makes quiet reps satisfying
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after ten minutes of tape review, he adds a cassette sticker and stops before inflating the task
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a cassette sticker sheet beside a waveform screen

exampleSpecs.domain: a dialysis patient recovering after a skipped weight log
exampleSpecs.audience: a patient who spirals when tracking breaks
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether never miss twice guides repair
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the nurse circles the blank square once and asks what will make tomorrow easy, not why yesterday failed
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a weight log with one circled blank square

exampleSpecs.domain: a ceramic kiln technician checking cone readings after a broken streak
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether tracking helps re-entry after disruption
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he reviews the missed firing log, adds the next cone reading, and protects the second day
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a kiln cone chart clipped to a warm brick wall

exampleSpecs.domain: a high-school debate coach using a visible return mark after missed speech drills
exampleSpecs.audience: a coach helping students recover from tournament fatigue
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the tracker signals come back today
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the student places a green return tab beside yesterday empty slot before giving one timed rebuttal
exampleSpecs.firstImage: green tabs on a debate drill board

exampleSpecs.domain: a fisheries officer tracking patrol reports through weather delays
exampleSpecs.audience: a field officer whose route breaks in storms
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether visible continuity survives missed patrol days
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after the storm blank, she files the next report by noon instead of waiting for a perfect week
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a rain-specked patrol map under a clear sleeve

skillTargets: recover after one miss before it becomes two

tryThisNowSpec: Mark one completed rep in a visible tracker. If yesterday is blank, mark today as the return instead of explaining the miss.
